text:
[Review] Montabi deserves more attention (Pokemon X Slay the Spire X Megaman Battle Network) Note: I am not affiliated with the studio; I'm just some old guy whose love for roguelike deckbuilders was rekindled by this game.

Introduction:

Montabi

I've played a lot of deckbuilders, OG Slay the Spire, modded Slay the Spire, Vault of the Void, Indie's Lies, Across the Obelisk, Roguebook, many lesser-known ones - and recently Slay the Spire II.

Especially coming from Slay the Spire II, Montabi was such a refreshing experience. Why? Some might crucify me for saying this, but Slay the Spire II always made me feel like I had no meaningful choices; no information about the enemies I would face other that they would be elites or not, no artifact selection - you just got something random, add to that weak nearly meaningless card upgrades - and ultimately just one deck to navigate with extremely limited card draw; I managed to do well consistently - but I felt like the game was mostly playing itself, and there was a lack of meaningful choices. It drove me away from the game and, nearly, the whole genre.

Now, to see why Montabi was such an incredibly refreshing experience, you need to understand what it is.

So, what is Montabi?
Montabi is a roguelike deckbuilder, where combat takes place on two 3x3 grids akin to Mega Man Battle Network. The map resembles Vault of the Void, it gives you a solid amount of information, in particular, which path leads to facing what creature, aside from shops, events, etc.
Every non-boss creature can theoretically be tamed, although you have a limited amount of tames per run.

In combat, you can have 2 creatures and a trainer on the field, as well as up to 3 creatures on the bench. There is an item that allows you to have 3 creatures on the field. Combat ends when your trainer dies. Creatures revive after a set amount of turns, but receive an injury card as a penalty. Damage can be blocked by shields, reduced by harden or (in most cases) completely avoided by moving to a safe tile - or pushing your opponent out of range. Moving to an occupied tile will swap places. Important: One per turn the trainer can swap in a benched creature. This can e.g., be used to tank damage for a squishier unit, extend your burst or provide utility such as stealing enemy armor or moving status effects from one creature to another.

Each creature has its own deck of cards that can be built and customized; usually those options revolve around 1 to 3 different "themes" per creature. Cards are selected upon level-up and can be skipped; on level 5 and 10 creatures evolve, giving you a selection of passive abilities to pick from.

All 3 trainers have a selection of 3 "charms" when they start a run. Each charm has a unique passive ability. Each trainer has a unique skillset. When starting a run, you can freely pick any of your unlocked creatures to accompany you. 3 trainers with 3 charms and 24 creatures, make 216 different starting combinations before you even set a foot on the map; surprisingly, many combinations actually make sense.

During the run you can acquire equipment, consumables and apply stickers to your cards, which add mostly generic effects (card draw, status effects, DMW, buffs, etc).

All of it works so well together, it's insane
Are you intimidated yet? A trainer, 3 onboard creatures, 2~3 spares, all with full deck and gear. So many genres mixed... OUF, that's overwhelming!

In a way, yes: But that's why the game has different levels with varying degrees of leniency.

While many deckbuilders often left me with the feeling. "Well, there really was much else I could have done at this point", Montabi really adds so many layers of depth, that I usually have to admit to myself - there was a better way.

After how bored out of my mind I was with Slay the Spire II, Montabi was everything I wanted and added even more elements I didn't know I needed from my roguelike deckbuilder.

Frankly, at this point I'd say it's not just a roguelike deckbuilder, it's a fully fledged tactics game with a deckbuilder skin. Even if you don't like deckbuilders, if you like tactics games, this might also be for you.

So, why am I posting this?
This game is so incredible; it is f'ing CRIMINAL that it's only sitting at 123 reviews. While 95% positive reviews speak a clear language, the overall player count seems quite low. The devs deserve so much more love! The game is a from a small studio from a small studio and seems to be COMPLETELY flying below radar. I'm not a big streamer trendsetter - but if you hear me, this game deserves to be the next big thing. It's a passion project done right, a unique mix of genres, super fun to play, and with a cool artstyle.

P.S.: No spoilers - but after beating the campaign, there's also a super heartwarming story about one of the teammembers. The devs seem to be great people and a great team.

EDIT:

Somebody seems to go through the topic and downvote every positive comment less than 10 seconds after they're posted, without ever engaging with what people wrote. If you read this, I am happy to discuss the game, I am not sure what anybody did to deserve the hate? You are free to voice disagreement, but his behavior does not seem constructive. EDIT II: Okay, apparently I offended a disgruntled MMBN hadcore fan by comparing the two..

SILENT HILL: Townfall - Notice: Game Update (Patch 1.4.0) System Changes
・Gameplay & AI Improvements for The Weight:

- Grab attacks now deal heavy damage instead of causing instant death on Story Mode and Normal difficulties.

- Searching behaviors have been improved to prevent The Weight from ‘camping’ in front of the player’s objective for long periods of time.

- Searching behaviors have been improved to prevent The Weight from repeatedly searching the same location and remaining there for long periods of time.

- Hunting behaviors have been improved to prevent The Weight from tracking the player too aggressively.

・Gameplay & AI Improvements for enemies:

- Enemy sensitivity to the sound of firearms has been reduced.

- Enemy sensitivity to the sound of the player while running has been reduced.

- Enemy sensitivity to the sound of the player entering a hiding space has been reduced.

- The frequency of enemy counterattacks after successful player attacks during melee combat has been reduced.

- With the exception of The Weight, grapple attempts from enemies while the player is actively blocking with a melee weapon have been removed.

- Players are now given more time to react to enemies after escaping a grapple.

・Puzzle Information Design Improvements

- A collectible manual for the "Remote Systems Control" console that can be viewed for quick reference while operating the console has been added.

- The pipe layout for the "Aux Line" puzzle has been updated to improve clarity.

Bug Fixes
・Fixed a progress-blocking issue in Part 5 where glass could prevent the player from entering the CEG Tower.

・Fixed an issue in Part 5 where the names of the Projector Slides could incorrectly display the same name.

・Fixed several areas where the player could go out of bounds and break the sequence of the game.

・Fixed an issue where the Letterbox option would not be visible when playing on an ultrawide monitor.

・Added missing key bindings for AZERTY keyboards.

・Improved frame pacing and further reduced instances of streaming stutter.

Hellraiser: A couple quick things before you start the game... or your suffering will be legendary. I'm a huge fan, got it way early this morning as soon as I saw it - and I just made it past the prologue...

Note, however, that this suffering was wholly self-inflicted.

I always start games on the highest difficulty - Do not do that, it's basically Hardcore mode, they do not provide save points... hard games make me all the more determined to beat it, so I spent all morning restarting the entire level 50 times because the last guy looked at me. There are normally saves along the way...

After coming to this revelation, I immediately saved, but saw 2 entries in the save slot in a subsequent save point, so 'why not delete the extra'. But there are two entries for your save... one for your entire playthrough, then the individual save slots under that - I deleted my entire playthrough save.

So back to the beginning I went, one last time...

Don't be like me kids.

Wine (for Linux) might mark dgvoodoo2 as WONTFIX due to malicious and intentional sabotage by developer to not run via Wine User Nostalgia_Realm used GPT-6 Astra to decompile dgvoodoo2 to check crashing of the utility on Linux/Wine environments

I used **GPT-6 Astra** to investigate the supplied dgVoodoo2 binaries. It identified the relevant code and produced a working fix in approximately **17 minutes**. I then personally confirmed that Snail Mail’s Tutorial renders and responds correctly with the patched DLL.

The findings point to **a Wine-specific code path inside dgVoodoo2 as the cause of this regression**. No changes to Wine were needed to remove the reproduced crash.

The relevant code does the following:

1. Walks the process’s loaded-module list and locates `NTDLL.DLL` using an encoded name.
2. Reads its export table directly and searches for names containing `wine_get`, such as `wine_get_version`.
3. Conceals that substring comparison behind arithmetic and numeric constants, rather than a readable Wine-identification string.
4. When Wine is detected, takes a path that skips clearing two graphics-state values. Redirecting execution to the normal clearing path removes the reproduced failure.

This was confirmed in **2.82 and 2.87.5**. The corresponding check was absent from the supplied **2.8** D3D8/DDraw binaries. Every intervening release was not individually analysed, so this does not establish the exact release that first introduced it.

The fix is very small once the affected DLLs are unpacked:

- **2.82:** change one branch-displacement byte in each affected D3D8/DDraw DLL so that the state-clearing instructions also execute under Wine.
- **2.87.5:** change one instruction byte per Wine-export detection routine so it returns “not detected.” There are **23 copies across 22 DLLs**, including both copies inside the ARM64X D3D9 DLL. The two D3DImm DLLs lack this check.

With the original DLLs, Snail Mail crashes and a separate DirectDraw test fails during surface creation. With the patches, Snail Mail runs and the DirectDraw test passes drawing, pixel readback, and cleanup. DXVK was still needed for D3D11 translation.

**I strongly suspect deliberate interference with Wine compatibility**, given the obfuscated Wine detection and the harmful path it selects. Intent cannot be established conclusively from this evidence alone, but the Wine detection itself, and its connection to the reproduced failure is concrete. The earlier comment’s more specific D3D12-pointer explanation was not independently established.

Folks Who Gave Up MP games for SP Ones, What Did You Do? A thought ive been sitting with for a while is giving up multiplayer games for single player ones. I have a massive backlog of SP games that I would love to get to, but the pull of multiplayer games, especially competitive ones like NS2 and CS2 is pretty strong because I like the idea of progressing and getting better at it over others and how each game/round is completely different and could require different techniques to complete.

The main reason Im wanting to give them up is I have twin toddlers and its much easier to quickly pause a SP game to change a dirty diaper or when one wakes up too soon from a nap than a MP game. Plus there a lot of great SP games with really interesting stories to tell like SOMA for example.

I know an obvious answer to this would be to uninstall the MP games and just play the SP ones, but im just curious about others who made that transition and what worked for them.
